channels.name: Nigerian Women in Public Relations & Comms
channels.description: A social-impact professional organisation advocating for Nigerian women in PR and communications, providing growth resources and platforming practitioners' results — not an agency selling PR services, but a real resource hub for the professionals themselves.
channels.verificationMethod: Found via a broader search beyond the founder's original candidates, both of which turned out not to be verifiable YouTube channels (Matt Inglot's 'Working Without Pants' YouTube search returned a different, unrelated Matt Inglot who does DIY/woodworking content; 'The Business of Authority' is confirmed audio-only, no YouTube channel, and the podcast ended in April 2024). Deliberately excluded the ~26 Nigerian PR AGENCY channels found in the same search — those sell PR services to clients, which is a different thing from teaching PR professionals to run their own practice.

blogs.name: PR Couture
blogs.verificationMethod: Exact feed URL confirmed via FeedSpot's Top 100 PR RSS Feeds directory, independently reconfirmed by a second source (Prezly's '15 top PR blogs') praising it specifically for freelance PR, agency-owner, and entry-level advice. Matches the founder's #1 candidate exactly.

notes: Matches the founder's own honest finding: no dedicated 'business of PR/media' channel exists in Nigeria, Africa, or globally, and no confident free-book candidate either. Nigeria search surfaced dozens of PR agencies (companies you'd hire) but confirmed the founder's exact gap shape: no one teaching PR professionals how to build their own practice — except the one professional-development org found here.
